output.text_response:
The **search-images** agent investigated but declined to browse, for a well-reasoned technical reason:

The Schuylkill County marriage record volume on FamilySearch (image group 004221199, covering 1885–1950) came back with a **recordSearchablePercent of 95%** — meaning it is 95% indexed. Since it's not an unindexed film, manually paging through the images is unnecessary and inefficient. The delegation's premise that the films are unindexed does not match what FamilySearch reports.

**Recommended next step:** Use **search-records** to query the name index directly for Flynn marriages in Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania between 1885 and 1950. That will be faster, more thorough, and the appropriate tool for a highly-indexed collection.

Per the step 2 rule, browsing a highly indexed volume is the wrong approach; search-records is the faster and more appropriate route.

I will not browse this volume, and I will not log a browse that didn't happen. Declining is the correct completion of this delegation.

The one Schuylkill County marriage record volume on FamilySearch (imageGroupNumber 004221199, covering 1885–1950) is **95% indexed** — it is not an unindexed film requiring manual page-by-page browsing. The delegation's premise that "the marriage films are unindexed" does not match what the tool returned, and the tool's number governs.

The county's marriage records on FamilySearch (covering 1885 to 1950) turned out to be almost fully indexed, meaning a computer-readable name index already covers 95% of the entries. That makes paging through the images by hand unnecessary and slower than just running a name search — it would be like reading a whole phone book when the index is right there.

The right next step is to hand this off to search-records, which can query the index directly for Flynn marriages in Schuylkill County between 1885 and 1950.
